question.text: An offshore fund domiciled in Mauritius invests into India. It has an Indian advisory office that scouts deals and recommends investments. The RISK being flagged when the scope of the advisory office is NOT tightly documented is:

answer.text: The Indian advisory office may be construed as a 'permanent establishment' (PE) or create 'place of effective management' (POEM) risk for the offshore fund in India
The Indian office automatically loses SEBI (AIF) registration
The offshore fund is barred from future FDI inflows
The manager must compulsorily register under SEBI (Portfolio Manager) Regulations

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 127 of the workbook, an Indian advisory office whose scope is not tightly documented may be construed as a permanent establishment (PE) of the offshore fund or may create place-of-effective-management (POEM) risk in India. The workbook stresses restricting the advisory office's scope through clear documentation. The Trap: SEBI deregistration, FDI bars and compulsory PMS registration are not the consequences flagged at page 127. Note: Drafting the advisory contract to restrict it to non-binding deal recommendations and ensuring final investment decisions are taken (and documented) offshore is the standard mitigation.
